bands.label: Strike and deal scramble
bands.summary: A US strike in the Gulf of Oman kills Indian sailors as Trump announces a US-Iran deal to be signed and the Strait of Hormuz set to reopen, with Iranian officials publicly contradicting the timing.

bands.label: After the 12-Day War
bands.summary: The June 2025 12-Day War between the US, Israel and Iran reshapes the region, with the death of Supreme Leader Khamenei, continued Israeli strikes on Lebanon, and a year of stalled negotiations leading into the anniversary.

bands.label: Maximum pressure era
bands.summary: Washington exits the nuclear deal and reimposes sanctions on Iranian oil, building up a Hormuz enforcement posture with recurring tanker seizures and incidents through the late 2010s and early 2020s.

frames.label: 10 June 2026 strike
frames.note: The story begins with the US strike in the Gulf of Oman that killed Indian seafarers aboard a tanker. Under this frame the situation reads as a sovereignty and accountability question: foreign nationals killed in international waters, families asking how the rescue was handled, and a foreign minister raising the deaths directly with Washington. New Delhi, the family of the Himachal sailor, and Indian outlets open here.

frames.label: 13 June 2025 12-Day War
frames.note: The story begins one year earlier with the opening of the 12-Day War between the US, Israel and Iran. Under this frame the tanker strike reads as another chapter of an ongoing armed conflict, with the anniversary, Khamenei's funeral and continuing strikes on Lebanon framing the incident as wartime, not enforcement. Tehran, Press TV and Iranian officials open with this anniversary date.

frames.label: May 2018 sanctions snapback
frames.note: The story begins with the US exit from the Iran nuclear deal and the snapback of sanctions on Iranian oil exports. Under this frame the tanker strike reads as enforcement of a long-running sanctions regime against suspected smuggling through Hormuz, with Secretary Rubio saying Hormuz violations will not be tolerated. Washington and US officials open here.
